module

public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Clique
@[expose] public section

namespace SimpleGraph
variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

open scoped Classical Finset List in

/-- A graph is a quasi-line graph if the neighborhood of every vertex can be partitioned into two cliques. -/
def IsQuasiLineGraph {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : V, ∃ (s₁ s₂ : Set V),
    s₁ ∪ s₂ = G.neighborSet v ∧ G.IsClique s₁ ∧ G.IsClique s₂


end SimpleGraph

reformulations.difference: The definition requires two cliques whose union is the open neighborhood, without requiring them to be disjoint. The docstring and Wikipedia use the word 'partition'; Chudnovsky–Seymour explicitly use 'union of two cliques'.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Given witnesses s₁ and s₂, replace them by s₁ and s₂ \ s₁. These sets are disjoint and have the same union, and the second remains a clique because every subset of a clique is a clique. Conversely, a disjoint clique partition is a clique cover. Parts may be empty, as required by the standard notion, which includes line graphs with isolated vertices and singleton neighborhoods. Proved the general ↔, without finiteness assumptions, as Review.quasiLine_iff_disjoint_partition in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The use site asks for a set s and the induced graphs on s and sᶜ, whereas erdosproblems.com asks for two vertex-disjoint subgraphs, not necessarily induced or covering all vertices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A complementary induced pair is a vertex-disjoint pair of subgraphs. Conversely, given vertex-disjoint subgraphs H and K, take s = V(H). There are graph homomorphisms from H to G[s] and from K to G[sᶜ], so the chromatic lower bounds are preserved. Proved this exact ↔ for arbitrary chromatic lower bounds as Review.partition_iff_disjoint_subgraphs in /workspace/review/use_site.lean. The BKPS09 abstract itself uses the induced-partition formulation.

review.notes: Checked the sole definition and its sole use site. #print confirms that the unused surrounding α/Fintype/DecidableEq variables do not become parameters of IsQuasiLineGraph. Mathlib's IsClique is pairwise adjacency of distinct vertices, and neighborSet is the open neighborhood; both have the intended meaning. No Mathlib duplicate or conflicting convention was found. Both scratch files compile without sorry. Tests cover empty and singleton types, complete and edgeless graphs (including infinite vertex types), K₁,₂, the claw K₁,₃, and the wheel with a five-cycle rim; the last two correctly fail. For the finite use site, also proved CliqueFree k ↔ cliqueNum < k. The Erdős page confirms the file's open main conjecture and solved partial-result statuses. BKPS09's full-text endpoints were blocked, but its institutional abstract states the exact result used; the definition was independently verified in the primary Chudnovsky–Seymour survey. No repository files were edited, and the target's blob hash matches the specified commit.
